question.text: Mr. Reddy invested Rs. 10,00,000 in an equity mutual fund. The NAV on 31 January 2018 was Rs. 12,00,000 (grandfathering date). He sold the units in March 2025 for Rs. 18,00,000. What is his LTCG under Section 112A after applying the grandfathering rule, but before applying the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption?

answer.text: Rs. 6,00,000 (Sale price minus higher of cost or NAV on 31 Jan 2018)

explanation.text: The Logic: For equity MF units acquired before 1 February 2018, Section 112A applies the grandfathering provision. The deemed cost of acquisition is the higher of (i) the actual cost (Rs. 10,00,000) or (ii) the NAV on 31 January 2018 (Rs. 12,00,000), capped at the sale price. Here the 31 Jan 2018 NAV (Rs. 12,00,000) is higher than the actual cost, so the deemed cost is Rs. 12,00,000. LTCG after grandfathering = 18,00,000 - 12,00,000 = Rs. 6,00,000. The Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption under Section 112A is applied separately when computing the actual tax liability; the question asks for the LTCG before that exemption. The Trap: Option A ignores grandfathering. Option C correctly computes net taxable LTCG (Rs. 6,00,000 - Rs. 1,25,000 = Rs. 4,75,000), but the stem asks for LTCG before the Rs. 1.25 lakh exemption. Option D applies the exemption to the un-grandfathered gain. Note: Source - NISM Series V-A Mutual Fund Distributors workbook (November 2025), p. 157, which describes the grandfathering rule and the Rs. 1.25 lakh equity LTCG exemption under Section 112A.
